newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Chinese Petroleum finds crude and gas.
newsitem.headline: Chinese Petroleum finds crude and gas.

text.p: Taiwan state-run Chinese Petroleum Corp's new oil well in northern Hsinchu county can produce crude oil and natural gas, a company spokeswoman said on Monday.
"This well can produce 90 kilolitres of crude oil and 80,000 cubic metres of natural gas every day," the spokeswoman said by telephone.
The Hsinchu well could have as much as 50 million cubic metres of natural gas and 63,000 kilolitres of crude oil in reserves, the spokeswoman said.
"This is a very rough estimate and could be different after we do a more detailled calculation," she said.
Chinese Petroleum started drilling the Hsinchu well in October 1996 and found the reserves in early February.
"We are drilling more oil wells in nearby areas because we believe there should be more reserves, mainly in natural gas," she said.
She declined to give further details about the find.
She said the discovery would not affect the state utility's crude and natural gas imports, which are under long-term contracts.
"What we find in the Hsinchu oil well or other wells will help supplies in the domestic market but definitely will not affect our imports," the spokeswoman said.
